maps.name: Using a hybrid museum guide
maps.context: A visitor enters a museum exhibition and uses a handheld guide device alongside physical labels, room signage, and a projected map.
maps.notes: This example includes physical, digital, spatial, and social parts of one interaction. Observed mappings describe what a visitor did during a walkthrough. Conceptualised mappings identify relationships that could be explored through a physical or Wizard-of-Oz prototype.

rows.description: Observed: The visitor picks up the device and holds it toward an artwork because its shape, screen, and camera opening suggest that it can be used to look at objects.
Observed: The visitor understands that aiming the device at an artwork should reveal information about that specific artwork.
signifiers: Artwork outline on the device screen
Alignment between device frame and artwork

rows.description: Observed: A short vibration and a change on the screen indicate that the artwork has been recognised.

rows.location: Physical room signage and projected map
rows.description: Observed: The visitor can see the exhibition title and room number on the wall, while the projected map shows the larger route through the exhibition.
Conceptualised: The device, projected map, and physical signs should use the same room names and directional language so the visitor can transfer understanding between them.
rows.change: Prototype the same route using paper signs, a hand-drawn map, and a simulated device screen.

rows.description: Conceptualised: The guide should limit the amount of audio information available while the visitor is moving, because too many choices may compete with attention to the physical exhibition.
rows.change: Test a simplified audio state that offers one recommended action at a time.

rows.location: Visitor asks a staff member for help
rows.description: Conceptualised: The system should make it clear when the visitor can stop using the device and ask a person for assistance rather than treating the digital guide as the only route.
rows.change: Explore a visible help point or staff prompt within the guide experience.
signifiers: Visible staff location on the projected map

rows.description: Conceptualised: A final physical and digital confirmation could help the visitor understand that the route is complete and show where they can return the device.
rows.change: Prototype a combined end state using a projected message, device screen, and return station sign.
signifiers: Change in device sound or vibration
